stories.headline: Uganda: Police Rescue 37 Suspected Human Trafficking Victims Police have rescued 37 children and young adults believed to be victims of human trafficking and arrested a bishop accused of recruiting them under the guise of
stories.summary: Ugandan police have rescued 37 children and young adults, aged 7-20, suspected to be victims of human trafficking. The victims, including 23 females and 14 males, were allegedly recruited by a bishop under false pretenses. Police launched an investigation into the suspected human trafficking operation after rescuing 18 children from a residential house in Kakunyu Village, Wakiso Town Council. Two suspects have been arrested in connection with the incident. The rescued children are students ranging from Primary One to Senior Five. The police are probing a suspected child trafficking network, with the bishop accused of recruiting the victims. The investigation is ongoing, with authorities working to uncover the extent of the trafficking operation and bring those responsible to justice.

stories.headline: 'America's doors are closed fully to asylum seekers': Supreme Court upholds Trump immigration policies US News: The US Supreme Court on Thursday allowed the Trump administration to strip hundreds of thousands of Haitian and Syrian immigrants of a humanitarian st.
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court ruled in favor of the Trump administration's bid to strip temporary protected status (TPS) from hundreds of thousands of Haitian and Syrian immigrants. This humanitarian status had protected them from deportation, allowing them to stay in the US for years. The court's decision gives the Trump administration the authority to rescind deportation protections for these individuals. The ruling is a victory for President Trump's hardline approach to immigration, following several other immigration-related rulings in his favor. The decision affects hundreds of thousands of people who were legally in the US and will now face potential deportation. The Supreme Court has consistently backed Trump's immigration policies, including deporting migrants to countries other than their own and revoking temporary legal status for hundreds of thousands of people.

stories.headline: Uganda: Health Minister Urges Early Treatment for Clubfoot, Rejects Witchcraft Myths LUWEERO -- The State Minister for Health, Anifa Kawooya, has called on health workers across Uganda to intensify community sensitisation on clubfoot and educate
stories.summary: Uganda's State Minister for Health, Anifa Kawooya, has urged health workers to intensify community awareness about clubfoot, a congenital birth condition that can lead to lifelong disability without early treatment. The minister warned that myths linking the condition to witchcraft and ancestral spirits are preventing children from receiving timely treatment. The National Clubfoot Program in Uganda offers a successful model for integrating rehabilitation services into health systems. The program uses the Ponseti method, a weekly treatment that can correct the condition if started early. The Ministry of Health aims to eliminate disability resulting from clubfoot and has called on health workers to educate communities about the importance of early treatment. World Clubfoot Day was recently celebrated in Uganda with awareness-raising and screening activities to promote access to life-changing treatment for affected children. Early treatment can significantly improve outcomes for children born with clubfoot.

stories.headline: Uganda: 'It's Me, Janet Museveni' - - First Lady Is Back The First Lady and Minister of Education and Sports, Mrs Janet Kataaha Museveni, has publicly spoken about her recovery from a serious health crisis, attributin
stories.summary: Uganda's First Lady and Minister of Education and Sports, Janet Museveni, has spoken publicly about her recovery from a serious health crisis. She attributed her survival to divine intervention and thanked Ugandans who prayed for her during her illness. President Yoweri Museveni recently re-appointed her as Education and Sports Minister, after revealing she had been battling a severe health issue. The First Lady expressed gratitude to her husband, referring to him as "Mzee", for leading the nation in prayer during her illness. Her recovery was marked with congratulatory messages from supporters and government officials. The President had earlier revealed her health scare as she marked her 78th birthday, prompting an outpouring of well-wishes and praise for her resilience. The First Lady's return to public life has been welcomed, with many attributing her recovery to the power of prayer.

stories.headline: Apple to skip high-end M6 Mac chips in favour of AI-focused M7 line
stories.summary: Apple will skip the high-end M6 Pro and M6 Max chips, instead focusing on the AI-focused M7 line. The company plans to release a base M6 chip for entry-level Macs later this year, but will not produce the higher-end M6 Pro, M6 Max, and M6 Ultra variants. According to reports, Apple's next Pro and Max chips will be part of the M7 generation, launching in 2027 with more advanced computing and graphics power. The M7 line is built around on-device AI, indicating a shift in Apple's chip development priorities. This decision suggests that Apple is accelerating its transition to the M7 family, which will reportedly offer enhanced performance and AI capabilities. The first M7 chips are expected to launch in 2027, marking a significant update to Apple's Mac lineup.

stories.headline: WhatsApp rolls out new warning feature to help users spot scammers
stories.summary: WhatsApp has introduced a new warning feature to help users identify potential scammers. The feature, available on both Android and iOS devices, displays a warning screen when a user attempts to start or open a chat with an unsaved phone number. Dubbed "Scam Alert," it aims to prevent users from engaging in risky conversations. When an unfamiliar number is detected, the app will display a warning inside the chat, alerting the user to potential scams. The feature is designed to make scam attempts from unknown numbers easier to spot, allowing users to avoid them before conversations begin. The rollout of this new security feature is part of WhatsApp's efforts to enhance user safety and protect against scams. The warning system is now available to users, providing an additional layer of protection against potential threats.

stories.headline: Gearing up for the Steam Machine? 5 Steam games players are eager to revisit
stories.summary: The upcoming Steam Machine is generating excitement among gamers, with many looking to build up their Steam Library. To prepare, players can explore compatible games, including classic titles from the Total War series, which will debut on PlayStation and Xbox for the first time with Total War: Warhammer 40,000. Meanwhile, an analysis of Steam's player numbers reveals the most played games. The Valve Index, a high-end virtual reality kit, launched at $1,000, raising questions about the potential price of the Steam Machine. As console gaming's future takes shape, a Steam Machine alternative has been unveiled, offering a glimpse into what's to come. With the Steam Machine on the horizon, gamers are eager to revisit popular Steam games and expand their libraries. Compatible games and new releases will be crucial to the Steam Machine's success.

stories.headline: OnePlus Nord Buds 4 unveiled with up to 54 hours of battery life, ANC
stories.summary: OnePlus has launched the Nord Buds 4 wireless earbuds in India, featuring 12mm titanium-coated dynamic drivers and spatial audio support. The earbuds offer up to 54 hours of battery life with the charging case, and a 10-minute charge provides up to 11 hours of use. They also come with 52dB Active Noise Cancellation (ANC) and run on Bluetooth 6.1 with a range of up to 250 meters. The Nord Buds 4 support Dual Device Connection, Google Fast Pair, and Microsoft Swift Pair, and are compatible with the Hey Melody app. The earbuds are priced at ₹3,300 in India, offering upgrades over their predecessor, including stronger ANC, longer battery life, and new AI-powered features. The total playback time is rated at 54 hours, making them a competitive option in the market.

stories.headline: ONE Championship: Imangazaliev eyes Muay Thai, kickboxing and MMA belts at flyweight
stories.summary: Asadula Imangazaliev, a Russian Muay Thai fighter, aims to hold belts in Muay Thai, kickboxing, and MMA at flyweight in ONE Championship. He previously competed for the vacant ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Championship but missed weight, allowing only Nong-O to be eligible for the title. Imangazaliev has impressed with his performances, including a knockout of Panpayak that earned him a six-figure contract. He is considered a top contender and has gained attention from notable figures in the combat sports world. With the flyweight Muay Thai belt still vacant, Imangazaliev is poised to make another run for the title, potentially facing top opponents at ONE Friday Fights. His goal is to dominate the flyweight division across multiple disciplines in ONE Championship.

stories.headline: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal FC want Bruno Guimaraes; Man Utd in Alvarez talks; Chelsea hijack; Liverpool latest
stories.summary: Arsenal FC is reportedly interested in signing Newcastle star Bruno Guimaraes, with the club having held initial talks with the player's agents. A formal approach has been made, with a potential deal valued at £55m. Guimaraes is currently impressing for Brazil at the World Cup. Meanwhile, Manchester United has started talks with Alvarez, while Chelsea is attempting to hijack a deal. Liverpool's latest transfer news is also being closely watched. The transfer window is active, with several major clubs pursuing key signings during the World Cup period. Arsenal's interest in Guimaraes is a significant development, with the Gunners seeking to strengthen their squad ahead of the new season.

stories.headline: Putellas decides to join London City Lionesses
stories.summary: Alexia Putellas has agreed to join London City Lionesses on a free transfer after leaving Barcelona following a 14-year spell. The move comes after Putellas allowed her Barcelona contract to run out. London City Lionesses are believed to have offered her substantial wages to secure her signing. Multiple sources have confirmed the agreement, which will see Putellas join the team this summer. Putellas' departure from Barcelona marks the end of an era for the Catalan giants, and her arrival at London City Lionesses is expected to be a significant boost to the team. The transfer is reportedly a free transfer, with no fee paid to Barcelona. Putellas is a highly experienced and decorated player, and her signing is a major coup for London City Lionesses.

stories.headline: USMNT player ratings vs Turkiye: Christian Pulisic returns, Sebastian Berhalter and Auston Trusty impress but late goal spoils perfect start
stories.summary: The USMNT lost 3-2 to Turkiye in their final group stage match, conceding a late goal in stoppage time. Auston Trusty scored his first international goal in the third minute, latching onto a Sebastian Berhalter corner kick. Christian Pulisic returned from injury, creating danger off the bench. Despite a heavily rotated lineup, the USMNT had a strong start, but ultimately fell short. Sebastian Berhalter impressed, providing the assist for Trusty's goal. The loss ended the USMNT's perfect start in the World Cup, but they will still move on to the Round of 32. The team's performance was marked by promising individual displays, including Pulisic's return and Berhalter's standout play. The USMNT will look to regroup and refocus ahead of their next match.

stories.headline: Delhi rape-murder horror: Cabbie waited 45 mins for asleep 10-year-old to separate from mother
stories.summary: A 10-year-old girl was kidnapped, raped, and murdered in south Delhi's Mehrauli. The incident occurred while she was sleeping beside her family on a pavement. The accused, a cab driver identified as Basu Kumar Singh or Babloo, allegedly waited for 45 minutes for the girl to separate from her mother before abducting her around 5 am. Her body was later found dumped in a forested area. The cab driver had reportedly driven past the spot nearly an hour before the abduction. Police have arrested the accused and are investigating the case. The girl's family was sleeping on the roadside when the incident took place. The accused's actions were premeditated, and the case has sparked outrage and concern over safety in the area. The investigation is ongoing, with police gathering evidence and building a case against the accused.

stories.headline: Pune Murder Accused Siya Goyal's Parents Siya Goyal's parents said that if their daughter is found guilty, then she should be pushed from the same place where Ketan was thrown from
stories.summary: Siya Goyal's parents have stated that if their daughter is found guilty of murdering her fiancé, Ketan Agarwal, she should be punished severely. They suggested that she should be pushed from the same location where Ketan fell to his death, Lohagad Fort in Pune. Siya is accused of conspiring with her alleged lover, Chetan Babulal Chaudhary, to kill Ketan. The parents claim they had no knowledge of any issues between the couple and that Siya never expressed displeasure about the marriage. They emphasize that if Siya is guilty, she should face strict punishment, even if it means death, with her mother specifically stating that she should be hanged. The family is currently dealing with the emotional aftermath, with Siya's father, Praveen Goyal, undergoing treatment at a hospital in Pune.

stories.headline: Mumbai local murder: Accused Roshan Suvarna came home drunk, cried after killing co-passenger
stories.summary: Roshan Suvarna, accused of murdering co-passenger Mayank Lohar in a Mumbai local train, allegedly committed the crime after a dispute over a trivial matter. Suvarna's family claimed he was intoxicated during the incident and returned home crying afterwards. He later confessed to the crime before leaving for Panvel. The dispute began when Suvarna opened the train door and was told off by Lohar, leading to a heated altercation. Suvarna pulled out a large knife from his bag and stabbed Lohar. The incident occurred around 6 pm, and Suvarna was later arrested by the police. The victim, Mayank Lohar, was travelling in the train when the dispute broke out, resulting in his fatal stabbing. Suvarna's actions were reportedly motivated by a sense of humiliation after being reprimanded.

stories.headline: Who is Mahesh Dixit? Doctor-turned-IPS officer to now head Intelligence Bureau Dixit succeeds Tapan Deka, and will take over after the latter's extended tenure ends on June 30
stories.summary: Mahesh Dixit, a 1993-batch IPS officer from the Andhra Pradesh cadre, has been appointed as the next chief of the Intelligence Bureau. He will succeed Tapan Kumar Deka, whose extended tenure ends on June 30. Dixit, a qualified medical doctor, has been serving as the Special Director of the Intelligence Bureau. The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved his appointment for a two-year term. Dixit has extensive experience in intelligence and law enforcement, having risen through the ranks since joining the IPS in 1993. He will take over as the chief of the country's premier intelligence agency, marking a significant milestone in his career. Dixit's unique background as a doctor-turned-IPS officer brings a distinct perspective to his new role as Intelligence Bureau chief.

stories.headline: The Geopolitics of SpaceX and Elon Musk Should one company—and one person—have this much power?
stories.summary: Elon Musk's influence extends broadly, with his ventures increasingly interconnected, creating a vast, vertically integrated entity. As CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, and cofounder of seven companies, including xAI, Musk's power is substantial. SpaceX, now a public company, debuted with a nearly $2 trillion valuation, with Musk owning 38% of the company. His track record with SpaceX launches and innovation has been strong, earning investor confidence. Despite being a polarizing figure, facing lawsuits and SEC investigations, Musk's impact on the tech and space industries is undeniable. With his companies' valuations and influence continuing to grow, concerns arise about the concentration of power in one person's hands, sparking debates about the implications of such dominance. Musk's success, built on his childhood dedication to reading and coding, has propelled him to the forefront of multiple industries.

stories.summary: The US Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that federal law allows the government to prevent asylum seekers from entering the country, effectively blocking their ability to apply for asylum. This decision was made on June 25, 2026. In other news, the community in Doral, where over 40% of residents are of Venezuelan origin, has come together to send aid to Venezuela after the country was hit by earthquakes. Meanwhile, news outlets such as Reuters and CNN continue to provide updates on the latest US and global news, including breaking developments in politics, health, and entertainment. These outlets also offer newsletters that summarize the biggest headlines of the day, keeping readers informed about current events. The ruling on asylum seekers is a significant development in US immigration policy.

stories.headline: Indian stock markets closed slightly higher on Thursday, marking a third consecutive week of gains, buoyed by falling crude oil prices.
stories.summary: Indian stock markets closed slightly higher on Thursday, marking a third consecutive week of gains. The Nifty 50 and Sensex both edged up, boosted by falling crude oil prices, which eased investor concerns. The Sensex and Nifty ended the holiday-shortened week higher by 0.39% and 0.18%, respectively. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, dropped 2.23% to $77.78 per barrel. Although crude oil prices rose to $77.33 USD/Bbl on June 19, they have fallen 21.30% over the past month. The markets are likely to remain driven by foreign investor activity, global cues, crude oil prices, and technical levels in the coming trading week. The recent gains come amid a significant development, as US President Donald Trump signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Iran to end the over three-month war, potentially impacting global oil prices.

stories.headline: Cooling crude prices drive weekly gains; Street expects Q2 earnings recovery
stories.summary: Crude oil prices have declined, driving weekly gains in the market. As of June 26, 2026, Crude Oil fell to $69.40 USD/Bbl, a 3.51% decrease from the previous day. Over the past month, the price has dropped 21.74%. Despite this, the current price is still 5.92% higher than a year ago. The decline in crude prices is expected to positively impact Q2 earnings, with the Street anticipating a recovery. The decrease in oil prices is being closely monitored by energy traders, analysts, and investment professionals, who are tracking market data, news, and events to inform their decisions. The price of Brent Crude and WTI oil futures are also being watched, as they provide key indicators of the energy market's direction.

stories.headline: The Indian stock market will remain closed on June 26 for the Muharram holiday.
stories.summary: The Indian stock market will remain closed on June 26 for the Muharram holiday. The National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) will observe a trading holiday, suspending trading in equity, equity derivatives, and currency segments. This closure will give investors a three-day break, including the weekend, with markets resuming on Monday, June 29. Commodity exchanges will have different schedules, with MCX resuming in the evening session, while NCDEX will remain shut. Several additional market holidays are scheduled later in the year. Investors should note this holiday when planning their trades for the week, as market sentiment is expected to be influenced by various factors, including US-Iran talks, upon the market's reopening. The holiday is part of the scheduled exchange holidays for 2026.

stories.headline: Benchmark indices extended their winning streak ahead of the holiday, with Nifty
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices extended their winning streak ahead of the holiday, with Nifty 50 closing at 24,056 and Sensex at 77,100.47. The gains were driven by easing crude oil prices and supportive measures for the rupee. The indices have been on an upward trend, with the Nifty reclaiming 24,250 and hitting a one-month high. The auto, FMCG, and realty stocks saw significant buying, contributing to the gains. The Sensex and Nifty ended the week with modest gains of around 0.3% each, supported by strength in banking, auto, pharma, and realty stocks. This marks the third straight week of gains for Indian equities, the longest winning streak in seven months, amid improving macro sentiment. The Nifty 50 rose 0.14% and Sensex added 0.14% in the latest trading session.

stories.headline: Former Meta exec sues over attempts to 'silence' her memoir Sarah Wynn-Williams accused the social media giant of trying to "silence" her after she published her memoir Careless People.
stories.summary: Former Meta executive Sarah Wynn-Williams is suing the company over attempts to "silence" her after publishing her memoir, "Careless People". Meta claims Wynn-Williams violated her non-disparagement agreement. The publisher, Macmillan, has expressed support for Wynn-Williams, stating they are "appalled" by Meta's tactics. A 57-page complaint was filed in a US district court, detailing Meta's efforts to stop Wynn-Williams from discussing her book. Meta obtained a ruling to restrict Wynn-Williams' comments, but she is now suing the company. The lawsuit is in response to Meta's actions, which Wynn-Williams alleges are intended to silence her and prevent her from sharing her experiences as a former Facebook policy executive. The case is ongoing, with Wynn-Williams seeking to overturn the restrictions and continue discussing her book.

stories.headline: Saudi Aramco resumes oil loading at Ras Tanura after 4-month halt By Florence Tan and Siyi Liu SINGAPORE, June 26 (Reuters) - Saudi Aramco resumed oil loading on Friday at its Ras Tanura terminal in the Gulf after a near four-
stories.summary: Saudi Aramco resumed oil loading at its Ras Tanura terminal in the Gulf on Friday, after a near four-month halt. Shipping data showed the resumption of crude loadings, marking a significant development for the world's biggest oil exporter. The terminal, a key facility for Saudi Aramco, had been idle for almost four months. The restart of oil loading operations comes as the company joins a rush to move cargoes. The move is expected to impact global oil supplies, with Saudi Aramco being a major player in the industry. Shipping data from LSEG confirmed the resumption of oil loading activities at the Ras Tanura terminal, indicating a return to normal operations after the prolonged halt. The development is likely to be closely watched by the oil market and industry stakeholders.

stories.headline: South Australia swings from three days of 100 pct renewables to worst drought in 7 years South Australia just experienced its worst wind drought in seven years.
stories.summary: South Australia experienced its worst wind drought in seven years, following three days of 100% renewables. The state's fleet of short-duration batteries went flat, and gas filled the gap. Australia's main grid recorded its worst one-day wind drought in over two years, causing price spikes in South Australia. This highlighted the need for more battery storage in the state, which has the highest penetration of renewables. South Australia sources roughly three-quarters of its annual electricity demand from wind and solar. The recent events underline the case for more and longer-duration battery storage to strengthen reliability in the grid. A new capacity mechanism has been implemented to address this issue, with the first tender for Firming Renewable Energy Microgrid (FERM) aiming to ensure reliability in the renewables-dominant power system.

stories.headline: Global Shapers discuss AI: How can we find our place in the age of AI? During the week of the World Economic Forum's Annual Meeting of the New Champions, widely known as Summer Davos, Global Shapers gathered to discuss AI, innovati
stories.summary: Global Shapers gathered during the World Economic Forum's Annual Meeting of the New Champions, also known as Summer Davos, to discuss the role of AI in shaping the future. The meeting emphasized the need for businesses to transform their workforce, operating models, and governance structures to maximize the value of AI. The World Economic Forum's flagship report, Youth Pulse 2026, provides insights from nearly 4,600 young people on issues including AI. The forum brought together over 84 world leaders, 800 CEOs, and thousands of others to discuss AI's impact on jobs, surveillance, and more. The Global Shapers' project aims to stimulate excitement and expertise towards responsible AI development and utilizing AI as a tool for a just and prosperous future. The discussions highlighted the importance of ethical AI development and its potential to shape a compassionate world.
